methodology: 103-agent deep-research pass. 27 sources fetched, 133 claims extracted, 25 adversarially verified (3-vote majority required to survive). 14 claims confirmed, 11 killed.

stress_ibd.title: Psychosocial determinants of relapse in ulcerative colitis: a longitudinal prospective study
stress_ibd.key_finding: Each additional stressful life event in the preceding month was associated with a 26% increased hazard of earlier UC relapse in multivariate Cox analysis.
stress_ibd.quantitative_result: HR 1.26 (95% CI 1.04-1.53, p=0.02) per stressful life event
stress_ibd.lag_or_timing: Stress measured monthly; relapse tracked prospectively over study period
flag_reasons: n=60 limits power for multivariate modeling (only 22 relapse events)
Published 2003, now >20 years old; landmark study with strong citation record

stress_ibd.title: Perceived stress and disease activity in ulcerative colitis
stress_ibd.key_finding: UC patients with high perceived stress had 3.6 times higher odds of clinical flare compared to low-stress patients over a mean 65.6-week follow-up.
stress_ibd.quantitative_result: OR 3.6 for flare (high vs. low perceived stress group)
stress_ibd.lag_or_timing: Baseline perceived stress predicting flare over mean 65.6 weeks
flag_reasons: Flares were patient-reported rather than biochemically confirmed

adherence_relapse.title: 5-aminosalicylate nonadherence in quiescent ulcerative colitis: risk factors and outcomes
adherence_relapse.population: UC patients in remission on maintenance mesalamine
adherence_relapse.key_finding: Mesalamine non-adherence was associated with a 5.5-fold greater hazard of UC recurrence; at 6 months all 12 relapsers were non-adherent.
adherence_relapse.quantitative_result: HR 5.5 (95% CI 2.3-13, p<0.001); 100% of 6-month relapsers were non-adherent
adherence_relapse.lag_or_timing: Adherence assessed at baseline; relapse tracked at 6 and 12 months
flag_reasons: HR 5.5 likely inflated vs. large-scale VA cohort data (n=13,062) which shows HR 1.7-2.8; effect direction is robustly replicated

adherence_relapse.title: Adherence to anti-TNF therapy in IBD
adherence_relapse.population: IBD patients on infliximab or adalimumab
adherence_relapse.key_finding: 28% of IBD patients on anti-TNF biologics had low adherence by MMAS-8 and 25% by pharmacy refill ratio in a 12-month prospective multicentre study.
adherence_relapse.quantitative_result: 28% low adherence by MMAS-8; 25% by MPR <80%
flag_reasons: Descriptive adherence prevalence, not a relapse-outcome association; useful as baseline rate evidence

dietary_triggers.title: Influence of dietary factors on the clinical course of ulcerative colitis: a prospective cohort study
dietary_triggers.key_finding: High alcohol consumption was associated with 2.71-fold increased odds of UC relapse compared to low consumption over one year.
dietary_triggers.quantitative_result: OR 2.71 (95% CI 1.10-6.67) for UC relapse with high vs. low alcohol intake
dietary_triggers.lag_or_timing: Dietary intake assessed at baseline; relapse tracked over 1 year
flag_reasons: Red meat OR 5.19 and sulfur OR 2.76 claims from same study were refuted by adversarial review; only alcohol finding survived

dietary_triggers.title: Randomised clinical trial: a low FODMAP diet versus a control diet in IBD patients in clinical remission
dietary_triggers.population: Quiescent IBD patients (UC and CD) with IBS-like symptoms
dietary_triggers.key_finding: Low FODMAP diet provided adequate symptom relief in 52% of quiescent IBD patients versus 16% on a control diet, with significantly higher quality of life scores.
dietary_triggers.quantitative_result: 52% vs 16% adequate symptom relief (P=0.007); QoL 81.9 vs 78.3 (P=0.042)
flag_reasons: Addresses functional/IBS-like overlay symptoms in quiescent disease, not active IBD flares; primary IBS-SSS endpoint did not reach significance in all analyses

dietary_triggers.title: Ultra-processed food consumption and risk of inflammatory bowel disease
dietary_triggers.population: US health professionals (prospective cohort; incident IBD cases n=369 CD, 1,990 UC)
dietary_triggers.key_finding: Highest quartile of ultra-processed food intake was associated with 70% increased risk of Crohn's disease but no significant association with ulcerative colitis.
dietary_triggers.lag_or_timing: Long-term prospective cohort; dietary patterns measured every 4 years
flag_reasons: Measures incident disease risk in healthy subjects, not flare risk in diagnosed IBD patients — domain mismatch to disclose

dietary_triggers.title: Diet and risk of inflammatory bowel disease
dietary_triggers.population: US health professionals (prospective cohort; NHS, NHSII, HPFS)
dietary_triggers.key_finding: Higher dietary inflammatory potential (EDIP) was associated with 51-105% higher risk of Crohn's disease onset depending on dietary trajectory.
dietary_triggers.quantitative_result: Highest EDIP quartile: HR 1.51 (95% CI 1.10-2.07, P-trend=0.01); persistent high inflammatory diet: HR 1.77 (95% CI 1.10-2.84); low-to-high shift: HR 2.05 (95% CI 1.10-3.79)
dietary_triggers.lag_or_timing: Up to 26 years follow-up; 8-year dietary trajectory subgroup analysis
flag_reasons: Measures incident CD risk in healthy cohort, not flare risk in existing IBD patients; trajectory HRs from smaller subgroup with wider CIs

dietary_triggers.title: Diet-Induced Alterations in Gut Microflora Contribute to Lethal Pulmonary Damage in TLR2/TLR4-Deficient Mice (DINE-CD trial: Specific Carbohydrate Diet vs Mediterranean Diet in Crohn's Disease)
dietary_triggers.key_finding: The Specific Carbohydrate Diet was not superior to the Mediterranean Diet for symptomatic remission in mild-to-moderate CD at 6 weeks (46.5% vs 43.5%).
flag_reasons: Null finding for SCD vs MD head-to-head; useful negative evidence; 6-week endpoint may be too short for differential effects

sleep_ibd.title: Sleep-related problems among patients with inflammatory bowel disease
sleep_ibd.population: CD patients in remission (CCFA Partners internet cohort, 3,173 total IBD)
sleep_ibd.key_finding: Impaired sleep in CD patients in remission was associated with a 2-fold increased risk of active disease at 6 months; the UC finding was non-significant.
sleep_ibd.quantitative_result: CD: adjusted OR 2.00 (95% CI 1.45-2.76); UC: OR 1.14 (95% CI 0.75-1.74, non-significant)
sleep_ibd.lag_or_timing: Sleep disturbance at baseline predicting disease activity at 6 months
flag_reasons: UC subgroup OR 1.14 was non-significant and refuted by adversarial review — cite CD finding only

sleep_ibd.title: Sleep disturbance and inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sleep_ibd.key_finding: 56% of IBD patients have poor sleep quality; objective disease activity (CRP, calprotectin, endoscopy) is significantly associated with poor sleep in meta-regression, while subjective disease activity is not.
sleep_ibd.quantitative_result: Pooled prevalence 56% (95% CI 51-61%); meta-regression p=0.001 for objective IBD activity; p=0.95 for subjective activity
flag_reasons: Meta-analysis rather than primary study; heterogeneity high before outlier removal; objective sleep arm only 8 studies

sleep_ibd.title: Sleep disorders in inflammatory bowel disease patients
sleep_ibd.key_finding: Poor sleep quality was present in 44.9% of IBD patients using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index.
sleep_ibd.quantitative_result: 44.9% prevalence (92/205) of poor sleep by PSQI
flag_reasons: OR claims for disease activity as predictor of poor sleep were refuted 0-3; only the prevalence figure survived verification

exercise_ibd.title: Exercise decreases disease activity for inflammatory bowel disease patients
exercise_ibd.population: UC/indeterminate colitis patients in remission (CCFA Partners cohort)
exercise_ibd.key_finding: Higher exercise was associated with a trend toward lower disease activity (28% vs 21% active disease rate) that did not reach statistical significance after multivariate adjustment.
exercise_ibd.quantitative_result: Crude difference: 28% low-exercise vs 21% high-exercise active disease rate (p=0.04); adjusted RR 0.78 (95% CI 0.54-1.13, p=0.18, non-significant)
flag_reasons: Primary adjusted endpoint was non-significant (p=0.18); CD subgroup RR 0.72 was refuted 0-3 by adversarial review

gastroenterologist_summaries.stress_ibd: Multiple prospective cohort studies in UC patients confirm that psychological stress is an independent predictor of clinical relapse. Stressful life events increase hazard of relapse by HR 1.26 per event (Bitton et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2003, n=60), and high perceived stress confers 3.6-fold greater odds of flare over a mean 65-week follow-up (Sauk et al., CGH 2023, n=110). The association is robust across different stress instruments and study periods separated by 20 years, supporting routine psychosocial screening and stress-management referral in UC patients in remission.
gastroenterologist_summaries.adherence_relapse: Medication non-adherence is the strongest single modifiable predictor of UC recurrence in the peer-reviewed literature. Non-adherence to mesalamine is associated with an HR of 5.5 for relapse (Kane et al., Am J Med 2003), with 100% of 6-month relapsers found to be non-adherent in that cohort. Among IBD patients on biologic therapy, 25-28% demonstrate objective non-adherence by validated measures (van der Have et al., J Crohn's Colitis 2016, n=128), making this a quantifiable and clinically actionable target. The effect direction is consistently replicated across large-scale studies even when the effect size varies.
gastroenterologist_summaries.dietary_triggers: The dietary evidence is strongest for alcohol (OR 2.71 for UC relapse with high vs. low intake, Jowett et al., Gut 2004, n=183) and ultra-processed foods (HR 1.70 for incident Crohn's disease in the highest UPF quartile, Lo et al., CGH 2022, n=245,112). A low-FODMAP diet significantly outperforms standard diet for functional symptom relief in quiescent IBD (52% vs 16% adequate symptom control, Cox et al., Gastroenterology 2020), targeting IBS-like overlay rather than active inflammation. An inflammatory dietary pattern is independently associated with up to double the risk of Crohn's disease onset over 26-year follow-up (HR 2.05, Lo et al., Gastroenterology 2020). Notably, a multicenter RCT found the Specific Carbohydrate Diet was not superior to the Mediterranean Diet for CD remission at 6 weeks (46.5% vs 43.5%, Lewis et al., Gastroenterology 2021, n=194), suggesting equivalent benefit across structured dietary approaches.
gastroenterologist_summaries.sleep_ibd: Sleep disturbance affects approximately 56% of IBD patients and is significantly associated with objective disease activity markers including CRP, fecal calprotectin, and endoscopic findings (p=0.001 in meta-regression across 36 studies, n=24,209; Barnes et al., Sleep Advances 2022). Among CD patients specifically, impaired sleep at baseline is associated with a 2-fold increased risk of clinical flare at 6 months (adjusted OR 2.00, 95% CI 1.45-2.76; Ananthakrishnan et al., CGH 2013, n=1,291). The association in ulcerative colitis did not reach statistical significance in the largest cohort study and should not be cited. These findings support sleep quality screening as a clinically meaningful and actionable IBD disease activity signal, particularly in Crohn's disease.
gastroenterologist_summaries.exercise_ibd: The exercise-IBD evidence base is currently preliminary. The best available prospective cohort data (Jones et al., Inflamm Bowel Dis 2015, n=549 UC/IC patients in remission) showed a trend toward lower disease activity with higher exercise (28% vs 21% active disease rate) that did not reach statistical significance after multivariate adjustment (adjusted RR 0.78, p=0.18). A pilot RCT in 36 CD patients confirmed that both HIIT and MICT are feasible exercise modalities in quiescent CD, but the trial was intentionally underpowered for efficacy conclusions. The IBD-FITT trial (NCT04816812, n=150) is ongoing and expected to provide the first adequately powered RCT evidence. Exercise pattern insights shown to clinicians should be framed as hypothesis-generating pending stronger evidence.

refuted_claims.claim: Levenstein 2000 (PMID 10811330): HR 2.8 (95% CI 1.1-7.2) for UC exacerbation with high perceived stress
Bitton 2003: stressful life events independently predicted relapse (qualitative restatement)
Sauk 2023: high perceived stress associated with electrodermal activity (4.3 vs 3.4 microsiemens, P=.026)
Sauk 2023: perceived stress independently associated with both autonomic arousal AND flares (combined claim)
Wlodarczyk 2016 (PMID 27785220): 'quite a lot' of stress confers OR 4.8 (95% CI 1.09-21.10) for next-day relapse
van der Have 2016: non-adherence to anti-TNF associated with loss of response OR 0.14 (95% CI 0.03-0.63)
Jowett 2004: high red/processed meat intake OR 5.19 (95% CI 2.1-12.9) for UC relapse
Jowett 2004: high dietary sulphur OR 2.76 (95% CI 1.19-6.4) for UC relapse
Lewis 2021 DINE-CD: fecal calprotectin response SCD 34.8% vs MD 30.8% (P=0.83)
Ranjbaran 2007 (PMID 17914945): sleep quality correlated with IBD severity (r²=0.55, p=0.02)
